clue.text: People with heeling powers!

parts.note: a pun on healing powers: these people put new heels on footwear, not cure the sick

explanation.surface: A tribute to faith healers with miraculous gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heeling' sounds like healing, so the clue seems to be about miracle workers; it is about cobblers mending heels.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobblers who mend shoes literally restore heels, so they have the power of fixing heels.

clue.text: Capital investment? This is the man to speak to

parts.note: he refers to a man
to address someone is to speak to them

explanation.surface: Want to invest capital? This is the fellow to talk to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means head, and an investment is clothing (what one is invested in), hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Headwear is literally what the head, or capital, is clothed in.

clue.text: A high-flier, English, age about 50

indicators.note: about means the word for age goes round the fifty

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An English high achiever is around fifty years old.
explanation.definitionFit: This bird of prey soars to great heights.

clue.text: The rest of the players

parts.note: not the other actors but the break the cast takes between acts of a play

explanation.surface: A remark about the remaining members of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' seems to mean the remainder; it means a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval between acts of a performance is when the actors have a break.

clue.text: Look for parking in a school enclosure

indicators.note: enclosure means the school's word surrounds the parking letter

parts.note: a school of thought is a sect
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Searching for somewhere to park within the school grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is the appearance or look of something.

clue.text: Having got the Right to decree reform, drawback

indicators.note: reform means the letters of to decree are shaped anew

explanation.surface: A ruler, empowered to reform by decree, finds a downside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' reads as a noun but defines as the verb draw back.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrocede is to move backwards or recede.

clue.text: A country's soldiery, almost all married

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of all is dropped

explanation.surface: A nation whose soldiers are nearly all married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims all to AL; ''s' is is, linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Some stars call on it notes may be provided

indicators.note: the letters of call on it notes may be provided in another order

explanation.surface: Stars that need notes from someone calling on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be provided' signals a rearrangement of CALL ON IT NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: A constellation is a recognised group of stars in the sky.

clue.text: Personal transport obtainable for coppers in days gone by

definitions.text: Personal transport obtainable for coppers in days gone by

parts.words: Personal transport obtainable for coppers in days gone by
parts.note: coppers seem to be police, but are the copper coins a Victorian cycle is named from

explanation.surface: Policemen in the past had their own vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' suggests police; the penny and farthing were old British copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian high-wheeled bicycle was named after its big and small wheels, like two coins.

clue.text: Flighty creature making a poet grin foolishly

indicators.note: grinning foolishly suggests the letters of the phrase are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A poet grinning like an idiot at some flighty creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges the letters of A POET GRIN; 'making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a butterfly, a creature that flits about in flight.

clue.text: Rush back East to do business

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for rush in the opposite direction

parts.note: to rush is to dart
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: Someone hurries back eastwards to get some work done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rush' looks like the definition but is the verb to dart; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell, carrying on commerce.

clue.text: Move to put trainee in a team

indicators.note: in places the learner's letter within the word for a team

parts.note: a side is a team
L, for learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A coach decides to put a youngster into the team.
explanation.walkthrough: L is from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to move furtively, edging sideways.

clue.text: Article on church or island personage providing a link

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
taken as written
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A grammar question about articles, churches and islands of some importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link placing the pieces one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who links the segments of a programme is the presenter at its centre.

clue.text: The French guys interrupting set out the essentials

indicators.note: interrupting means the French article and the guys break into the other letters
set out means the three letters are rearranged

parts.note: le is French for the
guys are men

explanation.surface: Some French blokes cut in while someone lays out the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into ETS, and 'interrupting' sends the French article and the guys between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic principles of a subject are its rudiments or fundamentals.

clue.text: Look on a political economist as 24 down

parts.note: an eye is a look
John Bright, the Victorian radical politician and free-trader

explanation.surface: A gaze cast on a political economist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link; 24 down's answer is a plant, so this is an example of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This small wild plant is part of a region's plant life.

clue.text: A blunt refusal to brush up — not for the first time

parts.note: re- means again, so not done for the first time
to buff is to polish or brush up

explanation.surface: Someone declines curtly to tidy up yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces come in reverse of their clue order: buffing again.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuff is a curt rejection or snub.

clue.text: Ridiculous rules vain general formulated

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters of rules vain are turned into nonsense and rearranged

explanation.surface: Absurd regulations, devised by a conceited general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like a military officer; it is the adjective. 'formulated' is a second rearrangement signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to all cases, all-embracing.

clue.text: Not yet licked into shape, but plainly a champion

explanation.surface: A rough work in progress, though obviously a winner.
explanation.definitionFit: Not yet beaten into form, and never defeated in competition, as a title-holder is.

clue.text: Told a story about a good man that's registered

indicators.note: about means the word for fibbing surrounds the saint

parts.note: to tell a story is to fib, to lie
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good man

explanation.surface: Someone spun a yarn about a virtuous man who had been put on record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told a story' is a euphemism for lying; ST (saint) is a crossword's good man.
explanation.definitionFit: Something listed is recorded on an official roll.

clue.text: Converting rear into front

indicators.note: converting means the letters of rear into are changed into another word

explanation.surface: A builder turns the back of a house into its facade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converting' rearranges the letters of REAR INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior describes the forward-facing part of something, as opposed to posterior.

clue.text: An orderly in Northern Ireland

parts.note: taken as written
trim means neat and orderly

explanation.surface: A hospital orderly working in Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' seems a hospital attendant; it is the adjective. ANTRIM is a county in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: County Antrim is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: To make a cut without hesitation shows open-mindedness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the cutting word goes round the hesitation

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Performing an operation decisively demonstrates a broad outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'shows' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance is a willingness to accept views other than one's own.

clue.text: One having some knowledge about a waterway

indicators.note: about means the knowledge goes round the letter for one

parts.note: lore is a body of knowledge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone with a little learning about rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river.

clue.text: Energetic man bound to back his leader

indicators.note: to back means the bound man is turned the other way

parts.note: a serf was a labourer bound to the land

indicators.note: his leader is the first letter of his

explanation.surface: A tireless man is tied to supporting his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SERF into FRES, and 'leader' takes H from 'his'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh describes someone lively and full of vigour, not tired.

clue.text: A girl's bloomers!

parts.note: bloomers seem to be underwear, but they are flowering plants, and the girl's name is the same word

explanation.surface: A cheeky reference to a young woman's underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests knickers; it means things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is both a girl's name and a collective term for plant life.

clue.text: Duck soar when unsettled

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: A duck takes off when disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird; it is the cricket score of zero, a round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is owing is outstanding, not yet paid.

clue.text: To a prison organiser it's for dealing with nasty lit le beasts

definitions.text: it's for dealing with nasty lit le beasts

indicators.note: an organiser rearranges, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A prison governor is handed something to deal with vermin in the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organiser' rearranges TO A PRISON; 'lit le' is the print's little.
explanation.definitionFit: This poison is a bait used to kill vermin such as rodents.

clue.text: Romantically directed, single folk agree

parts.note: sent means directed somewhere
I, the Roman numeral one
men are folk
to tally is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Unattached people concur that they are aimed at love.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sentimentally means acting with tender, mawkish feeling, as a romantic does.
